content.text: Understood. I will focus the history match on oil and water production rates and use pressure and gas rate as diagnostics for now. The historical well controls specify the liquid rate, so I will focus on the oil/water split, water breakthrough, and the later change in water cut. I will cease making field changes solely to reduce pressure or gas-rate errors.

Understood. The objective is to match field and individual-well oil and water production curves across the entire history, with no special priority for the end of the period. I will compare field FOPR/FWPR and well WOPR/WWPR errors together and use them to guide subsequent field changes. Pressure and gas rate will be excluded from selection for now.

By day 1488, round 1 raised the P14 water rate from about 1 to 200 m³/d, against a historical 862. P15 and P16 are still substantially low. The spatial simulation state also shows that water reaches P14 and P15 mainly by vertical flow in the lower intervals, while near the deepest P16 completion it moves along the layer. In the next round I will use this evidence to adjust porosity and permeability in the lower water-supply paths, retain the original composition, and continue testing against the oil and water curves.

The round 2 inputs have been generated. The original simulator is importing them for a rerun from the initial time. The changes concentrate near the lower parts of the wells and their bottom-water connections. Total pore volume decreases by about 0.68%. I have also saved the [round 1 partial-period oil and water comparison](<project>/experiments/compositional/jutul/results/oil_water_comparison_day1488.png). The full-period match cannot yet be judged from it.

Round 2 passed the original simulator's input checks. Active-cell mapping, well controls, initial pressure, and water saturation agree, and the per-cell component sum has zero deviation. To concentrate computing resources, I stopped the auxiliary permeability-only control and retained its first 1809 days. The baseline, full round 1 case, and round 2 oil/water case continue over the full history.

Over the common first 1488 days, field oil-rate and water-rate RMSE each fell from approximately 509.5 to 420.6 m³/d, an improvement of about 17%. Underproduction of water remains the main mismatch. Historical controls fix total liquid production, so the response to test here is the change in how the liquid divides into oil and water. Round 2 is testing the porosity and permeability changes designed for these mismatches.

The early round 2 results are in. Over the first 1281 days, P14 water-rate RMSE fell from 218 m³/d with the original fields to 63 m³/d. Water reached P15 and P16 too early. Their water rates at that time were 365 and 51, against historical values of 86 and 5. Round 3 will retain the P14 changes, reduce the enhancements to the lower P15 and P16 paths, and restore some pore volume to test whether breakthrough can be delayed.

Round 2 has spent more than 40 minutes on a 19-day report interval without producing a new report. Round 3 has reduced its oil and water mismatches in the common early window. I will retain the completed part of round 2 and its stop record and concentrate on validating the baseline and round 3 over the full period. Round 2 will remain marked as an incomplete experiment.
